title: 2022 AMC 12A Problem 13
statement: Let \(\mathcal{R}\) be the region in the complex plane consisting of all complex numbers \(z\) that can be written as the sum of complex numbers \(z_1\) and \(z_2,\) where \(z_1\) lies on the segment with endpoints \(3\) and \(4i,\) and \(z_2\) has magnitude at most \(1.\) What integer is closest to the area of \(\mathcal{R}?\)

solutions.text:
Adding a disk of radius \(1\) to every point of the segment sweeps out all points within distance \(1\) of it. The segment from \(3\) to \(4i\) has length \(\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5.\)

This “stadium” is a \(5\times2\) rectangle plus two half-disks of radius \(1,\) with area \[5\cdot2+\pi(1)^2=10+\pi\approx13.14.\]

The closest integer is \(13.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: \(\mathcal{R}\) is the set of all points within distance \(1\) of the segment
The segment has length \(5,\) so \(\mathcal{R}\) is a \(5\times2\) rectangle capped by two half-disks
